steps.title: Frame the task and authority boundary
steps.text: A customer-operations specialist selects accounts and asks for suggested lifecycle-stage changes. The proposal may recommend moving accounts from onboarding to active, at-risk, or collections, but it is advice only. The browser must never infer permission from generated text. Product services remain authoritative for account versions, action eligibility, execution, and the final outcome of every record.

steps.title: Make evidence review concrete
steps.text: Each proposed row shows its current and suggested stage, last-activity timestamp, open-invoice amount and age, evidence freshness, and a short explanation. The specialist can open the source record, remove a row, or change its proposed stage. Missing, stale, or restricted evidence is explained beside that account and prevents approval for that row without erasing the rest of the review.

steps.title: Separate generated content from eligibility
steps.text: Parse model output into GeneratedProposalContent, then pair it with a server-owned ActionEligibility result inside a ProposalEnvelope. ReviewState holds the specialist's selection and edits without mutating the cached proposal. Before enabling Approve, derive eligibility from current permission, proposal version, evidence versions, and record versions. A refresh rebases untouched rows while preserving and clearly marking local edits that need another look.

steps.title: Approve one exact command and reconcile each result
steps.text: Approval creates one idempotent ApprovalCommand containing the reviewed proposal version, evidence versions, selected account IDs, intended stage per account, and expected record revisions. The pending UI is not success. ActionOutcome returns a result for every account, so succeeded, conflicted, permission-denied, and failed rows stay visible separately with an audit reference and a precise next action.

steps.title: Handle Cancel, rollback, and accessibility truthfully
steps.text: Cancel records intent to stop waiting or asks the service to cancel; it does not prove execution stopped. A late mixed result still replaces the pending state. Only confirmed, reversible successes can offer a separate rollback command, which rechecks the latest record revision. Announce lifecycle changes in concise status messages, retain keyboard focus near the affected row, and never stream generated tokens into a live region.

blocks.title: Scope and user impact
rows: The affected row is paused with old and current evidence identified
The specialist keeps their work without unknowingly approving stale facts
Seven confirmed changes and three recovery rows
The result is useful without overstating completion
Cancel remains pending until the authoritative outcome arrives
The interface does not promise that account data was untouched

blocks.text: The frontend owns selection, evidence display, local edits, confirmation, focus, and recovery. The server is an abstract contract for proposal generation, permission, mutation, audit, and rollback eligibility.
